correctness.rationale: Every smooth curve corresponds to exactly one cubic-mask class with W^3 coefficient one among 32768 candidates. Two-chart Jacobian elimination is proved over the algebraic closure and recast as exact polynomial gcds. The fifteen rational plane contact criteria are exact binary cubics/sextics, and the full 48-element automorphism action identifies 274 smooth classes. The separate finite-extension checker reproduces all 36 joint contact strata, and exact Groebner ideals agree for 752 orbit representatives. The three six-plane orbits have size 48 each, and the explicit witness passes all six contact tests.

The sharp bound is specifically for rank-three canonical quadrics, disjoint from rank-four classes.

evidence: The 2017 construction implies cone-ruling planes have double contact, but not whether a given rational plane has three distinct contacts or how many transverse rational planes do.

Accessible prior same-topic curve claims treat rank-four split and nonsplit quadrics, whereas this claim treats the rank-three cone; a smooth nonhyperelliptic genus-four canonical curve has a unique containing quadric.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The ruling construction only supplies the three potential rational cone-tangent planes and cannot imply at most three *additional* proper transverse planes, exactly 144 maximizers, or their three projective classes. Previously determined rank-four contact spectra do not imply a rank-three contact spectrum because the canonical quadric rank is invariant under isomorphism.

Both formulations were searched; no equivalent six-plane sharp bound, complete distribution, or three extremal classes was encountered.

originality.rationale: The new invariant is the complete proper rational hyperplane contact spectrum on the binary rank-three canonical quadric cone, including a sharp six-plane bound and three exceptional classes. The inspected genus-four census does not provide this spectrum; the 2017 tritangent paper gives only a general contact family, and related rank-four claims have disjoint canonical quadric type. Exact scientific searches found no equivalent statement, but priority is not mathematically proven.
residual_risks: An unpublished computation or unindexed table could already tabulate the same proper-contact invariant.
The 2020 curve census supplies enough model data that the contact spectrum could have been computed later without independent publication.
Published papers use multiple conventions for tritangent: the present result intentionally includes the ruling-tangent planes and must not be compared to odd-theta-only counts.
Research-record search results were not independently authenticated as an exhaustive coverage of all mathematical publications.

value.rationale: The full contact spectrum of canonical genus-four curves on the binary cone, distinguishing its forced ruling contact planes from transverse contact planes, is a natural projective and theta-geometric invariant not fixed by curve counts or point numbers. The unexpectedly sharp maximum of six, all three exceptional isomorphism classes, and pointfree maximizer give a substantive complete finite classification. This is not merely a coefficient normalization or a recomputation of an existing rational-point table.
